messages:
maria: noticing a big throughput drop on prod-dedicated-us-west-2. pods repeatedly restart, tail shows OOMs on the runtime-worker processes. 50% drop in p95 qps since 08:10 UTC. anyone looking?
kevin: saw it, I'm on it. grabbing logs now. `kubectl get pods -n redwood | grep runtime` shows several `CrashLoopBackOff` on pool-gpu-3.
kevin: `kubectl logs runtime-worker-3 -n redwood --previous` -> repeated CUDA OOM: \n```
kevin: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512 MiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity; 30.8 GiB already allocated; 512 MiB free)
kevin: ```
jonathan: interesting — allocation numbers look normal but fragmentation seems high. saw similar pattern when kernel-selector fell back to generic matmul in last week's rollout. did we flip the selector heuristics at 07:50?
sasha: profiling snapshot from 08:12 attached: KV cache eviction rate spiked to 3k/s, average batch size down from 12 to 3, and continuous small allocations in allocator slab arenas. flamegraph shows heavy time in `copy_to_device` and `alloc_slab` paths.
kevin: pinging the runtime logs for kernel decisions: `kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_fp32_generic (fallback), reason=unsupported_fp16_path` repeated. that explains extra memory.
maria: so fallback -> bigger kernels -> more memory -> fragmentation -> OOM -> worker restart -> cache misses -> more cold starts and smaller batches -> throughput drop.
sasha: yes. KV cache churn is making it worse: eviction churn causes lots of small allocations, frees, and long tail fragmentation. allocator stats: `slab_free_ratio` dropped from 0.48 -> 0.12.
dave: deploy-bot: @maria @kevin detected increased restarts on runtime-worker pool-gpu-3. rolling back recent kernel-selector commit is allowed. do you want me to trigger rollback? :warning:
kevin: let's hold rollback 1m, trying quick mitigations: 1) disable autoscale to avoid cascading restarts, 2) set env `FORCE_KERNEL=preferred_fp16` on pool-gpu-3 to force selector to use FP16 kernels where safe, 3) increase slab_coalesce_threshold to reduce fragmentation.
jonathan: note: forcing FP16 can fail for a tiny subset of models that rely on fp32 kernels. we should update routing policy to fallback to a dedicated fp32 pool for those requests.
maria: executing step 1 and 2 now. `kubectl set env ds/runtime-worker FORCE_KERNEL=preferred_fp16 -n redwood` and `kubectl scale deployment runtime-worker --replicas=6 -n redwood` (scale down autoscaling).
kevin: after env set, observed kernel_selector logs flip back to `chosen_kernel=matmul_fp16_optimized` and CUDA memory usage per process dropped ~20%. fragmentation still high but fewer OOMs.
sasha: eviction rate dropping slowly, batch size creeping back to ~8. flamegraph still shows some alloc churn but much lower.
maria: rolling restart of the remaining crashloop pods to clear bad alloc state: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime-worker -n redwood`
dave: deploy-bot: rollout restart initiated by maria.
kevin: post-restart metrics: worker restarts almost stopped, p95 latency back within 10% of baseline, throughput at ~88% recovering. no new OOMs in last 6m.
jonathan: root cause summary so far: recent kernel-selector heuristic change allowed more fallbacks to generic fp32 kernels under certain sequence-length distributions. those kernels allocate larger temporaries, interacting badly with our slab allocator under high KV eviction churn -> memory fragmentation -> OOM cascades -> restarts. noisy tenant (high eviction churn) amplified the effect.
sasha: preliminary mitigations: revert kernel-selector heuristic (short-term), add allocation coalesce and increase slab reclaim aggressiveness, route known high-churn workloads to specialized nodes, and add a guard in selector to avoid generic fp32 fallback during high-fragmentation signals.
maria: immediate action items: (1) keep FORCE_KERNEL on pool-gpu-3 until safe rollback (kevin), (2) open postmortem and add perf test that simulates KV churn + kernel fallback (jonathan), (3) add allocator metrics and an SLO for slab_free_ratio (sasha). I'll create an incident doc.
kevin: opened ticket INF-2392 to track rollback and config changes. linking logs and profiler traces.
jonathan: will revert the selector heuristic in a canary branch, test against churn harness, and coordinate a safe rollout.
sasha: I'll add the allocator telemetry dashboard and alert on `slab_free_ratio < 0.2`.
maria: thanks team. keeping this thread pinned to incident channel. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: incident-stamp: 2026-03-18T09:10:00Z
